submission.natural_language_explanation: The pole is a retrospective detector for a rare, out-of-place word-piece: it fires when the current token is an uncommon piece of vocabulary - a non-English or accented letter/word (İşte, جبل, いち, bonne, kan), a code or technical literal (bootstrap, override, usr, .nav, cdnjs, GV), an all-caps identifier (LOUD, BOOL, ÜN), a rare proper noun (Kuwait, Massachusetts, Vermont) or low-frequency open-class vocabulary (chemotherapy, transplantation, conference, interview) - and reads ~0 on the highest-frequency English words (' the', ' of', ' a', ' and', ' is', ' can', ' people', ' home'), on digits, and on whitespace/newline-only tokens. The preceding token gates this rather than causing it: the very same literal is strong after a boundary ('print(bootstrap)' 0.82, 'print(aced)' 1.04, 'print( override)' 0.55, 'Q:\n\n override' 0.93) but near zero after an ordinary word or a closing bracket ('the function bootstrap(x)' 0.00, 'print)bootstrap)' 0.07), while merely uncommon English words such as ' actually' and ' support' form a weaker 0.2-0.3 band that fires after any word (0.31 / 0.22) and is silent after a comma (0.00); the ragged edge I cannot yet predict is a minority of mid-frequency function words that do fire (' when' 0.16, ' whether' 0.14) and common content words that do not (' because' 0.02, ' very' 0.00), and the neuron's opposite (positive) pole peaks on the most frequent function words, digits and the closers ')', ']' and '}'.
